facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Yutyrannus.
facts.quote: genus: Yutyrannus

facts.statement: The only known species is Yutyrannus huali.
facts.quote: species: huali

facts.statement: The genus was described by Xu and colleagues in 2012.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Xu et al., 2012

facts.statement: Yutyrannus is a proceratosaurid tyrannosauroid dinosaur meaning "feathered tyrant".
facts.quote: Yutyrannus (meaning "feathered tyrant") is a genus of proceratosaurid tyrannosauroid dinosaur

facts.statement: Yutyrannus lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now northeastern China.
facts.quote: This species lived during the early Cretaceous period in what is now northeastern China

facts.statement: Three fossils found in Liaoning Province are the largest dinosaur specimens preserving direct evidence of feathers.
facts.quote: Three fossils of Yutyrannus huali — all found in the rock beds of Liaoning Province — are the largest-known dinosaur specimens that preserve direct evidence of feathers

facts.statement: Xu Xing and colleagues named and described Yutyrannus huali in 2012.
facts.quote: Yutyrannus huali was named and scientifically described in 2012 by Xu Xing et al.

facts.statement: The name combines the Chinese word for feather and the Greek word for tyrant.
facts.quote: The name is derived from Mandarin Chinese yǔ (羽, "feather") and Latinised Greek tyrannos (τύραννος, "tyrant")

facts.statement: Three nearly complete specimens representing an adult, subadult, and juvenile are known.
facts.quote: Yutyrannus is known from three nearly complete fossil specimens (an adult, a subadult and a juvenile)

facts.statement: The fossils likely come from the Barremian Yixian Formation, approximately 125 million years old.
facts.quote: They were thus probably found in a layer of the Yixian Formation, dating from the Barremian, approximately 125 million years old

facts.statement: Yutyrannus was a large bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Yutyrannus was a large bipedal predator

facts.statement: The largest known specimen is estimated to be 10 meters long and weigh about 1414 kilograms.
facts.quote: The holotype and oldest-known specimen has an estimated length of 10 m and an estimated weight of about 1414 kg

facts.statement: The skull of the largest specimen is estimated to be 90.5 centimeters long.
facts.quote: Its skull has an estimated length of 90.5 cm

facts.statement: The preserved feathers were long, reaching up to 20 centimeters, and filamentous.
facts.quote: The feathers were long, up to 20 cm, and filamentous

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the feathers may have covered the whole body to regulate temperature in a climate with an average annual temperature of 10 degrees Celsius.
facts.quote: Based on the distribution of the feathers, they may have covered the whole body and served in regulating temperature, given the rather cold climate of the Yixian with an average annual temperature of 10 C

facts.statement: Some researchers previously hypothesized that the structures might be ancestral filamentous structures rather than true feathers.
facts.quote: It was considered possible that the integumentary structures of Yutyrannus might not represent true feathers and represent filamentous structures, being ancestral state to feathers

facts.statement: All phylogenetic analyses classify Yutyrannus within the group Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: To date, all phylogenetic analyses of Yutyrannus relationships have classified it in the group Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis by Carr and Brusatte placed Yutyrannus within the family Proceratosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2016, a phylogenetic analysis conducted by Thomas Carr and Stephen Brusatte re-examined the evolutionary relationships of the Tyrannosauroidea. Their analysis found Yutyrannus to be more basal than Dilong, placing it within the family Proceratosauridae

facts.statement: The skull grew more robust and deeper during growth.
facts.quote: The skull, on the other hand, grew more robust and deeper

facts.statement: A 2018 study indicates Yutyrannus had a simple hyoid structure and a flat tongue like a crocodile.
facts.quote: According to a 2018 study, Yutyrannus had a simple hyoid structure, indicating it had a flat tongue, like a crocodile

facts.statement: A 2023 study estimated the bite force at 2,405 Newtons (540 pounds-force).
facts.quote: The bite force of Yutyrannus was estimated to be 2,405 N (540 lbf) according to a 2023 study

facts.statement: Some paleontologists interpret Yutyrannus as a pack hunter because the three known individuals were allegedly found together.
facts.quote: Because the three known individuals of Yutyrannus were allegedly found together, some paleontologists, including Xu Xing, have interpreted the animal as a pack hunter

facts.statement: Xu Xing speculated that Yutyrannus may have hunted sauropods based on sauropod material found in the same quarry.
facts.quote: Based on the presence of sauropod material in the quarry in which the three specimens were found, Xu has further speculated that Yutyrannus may have hunted sauropods

facts.statement: Age estimates suggest Yutyrannus originated from the Lujiatun or Jianshangou beds of the Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: Age estimates point towards Yutyrannus originating from the Lujiatun or the Jianshangou beds of the Yixian

facts.statement: Yutyrannus was likely an apex predator.
facts.quote: It was likely an apex predator

facts.statement: The environment was comparable to modern temperate rainforests of British Columbia with significant seasonal temperature changes.
facts.quote: The environment would have been comparable to the modern day temperate rainforests of British Columbia, and would have experienced significant seasonal changes in temperature

facts.statement: Yutyrannus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 125 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 millones de años durante el Aptiense, en lo que ahora es Asia

facts.statement: Fossils of Yutyrannus have been found in Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles han aparecido en la provincia de Liaoning, China

facts.statement: At nearly 9 meters long, Yutyrannus huali is the largest known feathered dinosaur.
facts.quote: Con sus cerca de 9 metros de longitud, Y. huali es el mayor dinosaurio con plumas conocido

facts.statement: The holotype and oldest known specimen of Yutyrannus measured 9 meters in length and weighed an estimated 1,414 kilograms.
facts.quote: El holotipo y el ejemplar de más edad conocido, tiene una longitud de 9 metros y un peso estimado de 1414 kg

facts.statement: The skull of Yutyrannus has an estimated length of 905 millimeters.
facts.quote: Su cráneo tiene una longitud estimada de 905 milímetros

facts.statement: The snout features a high midline crest formed by nasal and premaxillary bones containing large pneumatic cavities.
facts.quote: El hocico tiene una alta cresta de la línea media, formado por los huesos nasales y el premaxilar que están ocupados por grandes cavidades neumáticas

facts.statement: The feathers of Yutyrannus were long, reaching up to 20 centimeters, and filamentous.
facts.quote: Las plumas eran largas, de hasta 20 centímetros (7,9 pulgadas) y filamentosas

facts.statement: Yutyrannus huali is currently the largest known dinosaur species with direct evidence of feathers, being forty times heavier than the previous record holder, Beipiaosaurus.
facts.quote: Y. huali es actualmente la mayor especie conocida de dinosaurios con una prueba directa de plumas, cuarenta veces más pesado que el anterior poseedor del récord, Beipiaosaurus

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ZCDM V5000 had tail feathers pointing backward at a 30-degree angle relative to the tail axis.
facts.quote: El espécimen ZCDM V5000 tenía plumas en la cola apuntando hacia atrás en un ángulo de 30° con el eje de cola

facts.statement: Based on feather distribution, Yutyrannus was likely covered all over its body to regulate temperature in the cold Yixian climate, which had an average annual temperature of 10°C.
facts.quote: Con base en esta distribución, se puede inferir que estaba cubierto todo el cuerpo y que servía en la regulación de la temperatura, dado el clima más frío de Yixian con una temperatura media anual de 10 °C

facts.statement: The two adult specimens had distinctive wavy crests on their snouts flanking a raised central crest, likely used for display.
facts.quote: Además, los dos ejemplares adultos tenían distintivas, crestas "ondulada" sobre sus hocicos, a ambos lados de una cresta elevada central, que probablemente se usaron para su visualización

facts.statement: Yutyrannus was named in 2012 by Xu Xing, Kebai Wang, Zhang Ke, Qingju Ma, Xing Lida, Corwin Sullivan, Dongyu Hu, Shuqing Cheng, and Wang Shuo.
facts.quote: nombrada en 2012 por Xu Xing, Kebai Wang, Zhang Ke, Qingju Ma, Xing Lida, Corwin Sullivan, Dongyu Hu, Shuqing Cheng y Wang Shuo

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Chinese character for 'feather' and the Greek word for 'tyrant', referencing its status as a feathered tyrannosaurid.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del chino mandarín Yu ,羽, "pluma" y τύραννος la forma griega latinizada de tyrannos, "tirano"

facts.statement: The specific name derives from the Chinese word for 'beautiful', referring to the beauty of its plumage.
facts.quote: El nombre específico deriva del mandarín huali ,华丽, "bello", en referencia a la belleza de su plumaje

facts.statement: Yutyrannus is known from three nearly complete fossil specimens representing an adult, a subadult, and a juvenile.
facts.quote: Yutyrannus se conoce a partir de tres especímenes fósiles casi completos, un adulto, un subadulto y juvenil

facts.statement: The fossils had been cut into pieces the size of bath mats, facilitating transport by two people.
facts.quote: Los fósiles habían sido cortados en trozos del tamaño de las alfombrillas de baño, lo que facilitaba su transporte por dos personas

facts.statement: Yutyrannus was assigned to Tyrannosauroidea by its describers in 2012.
facts.quote: Yutyrannus fue asignado por sus descriptores a Tyrannosauroidea en 2012

facts.statement: Its basal traits include long arms with three fingers and a short foot lacking an arctometatarsus.
facts.quote: Sus rasgos basales incluyen los largos brazos con tres dedos y un pie corto sin el arctometatarso

facts.statement: During growth, the lower legs, feet, ilia, and forelimbs became relatively smaller in Yutyrannus.
facts.quote: Durante el crecimiento, la parte inferior de las piernas, los pies, los ilíacos y las extremidades anteriores se hicieron relativamente más pequeños

facts.statement: Conversely, the skull became more robust and deep during growth in Yutyrannus.
facts.quote: El cráneo, por otro lado, se hizo más robusto y profundo

facts.statement: According to a 2018 study, Yutyrannus had a simple hyoid structure indicating a flat tongue, similar to a crocodile.
facts.quote: Según un estudio de 2018, Yutyrannus tenía una estructura hioides simple, lo que indica que tenía una lengua plana , como un cocodrilo

facts.statement: It is debated whether the skin of later tyrannosaurids developed scales secondarily in response to body size, warmer climates, or other factors.
facts.quote: Si la piel escamosa era el rasgo epidérmico dominante de los géneros posteriores, entonces la extensión y la naturaleza de la cubierta tegumentaria pueden haber cambiado con el tiempo en respuesta al tamaño del cuerpo, un clima más cálido u otros factores

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest the integumentary structures of Yutyrannus might not represent true feathers but ancestral filamentous structures, though this hypothesis has been refuted by later research.
facts.quote: Es posible que las estructuras tegumentarias de Yutyrannus no representen plumas verdaderas y representen estructuras filamentosas, siendo un estado ancestral de las plumas

facts.statement: Some paleontologists, including Xu Xing, suggest that Yutyrannus hunted in packs because the three known individuals were found together.
facts.quote: Debido a que los tres individuos conocidos de Yutyrannus supuestamente fueron encontrados juntos, algunos paleontólogos, incluido Xu Xing, han interpretado al animal como un cazador en manada.

facts.statement: Xu Xing speculates that Yutyrannus may have hunted sauropods and that the three known specimens died during such a hunt.
facts.quote: Xu ha especulado además que Yutyrannus pudo haber cazado saurópodos y que los tres individuos conocidos pudieron haber muerto mientras lo hacían.

facts.statement: The true cause of death for the known Yutyrannus specimens remains unknown.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, se desconoce la verdadera causa de su muerte.

facts.statement: The environment where Yutyrannus lived was comparable to modern temperate tropical rainforests in British Columbia and experienced significant seasonal temperature changes.
facts.quote: El medio ambiente habría sido comparable a las selvas tropicales templadas de hoy en día de la Columbia Británica, y habría experimentado cambios estacionales significativos en la temperatura.

facts.statement: Yutyrannus belongs to the parent group Proceratosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Proceratosauridae

facts.statement: Yutyrannus is classified within the family Proceratosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Proceratosauridae

facts.statement: Yutyrannus lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, during the Barremian to Aptian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)
